name: Eggs Hawaii / Ka Lei Eggs
organizer: Eggs Hawaii (Ka Lei Eggs / Hawaiian Maid Eggs)
notes: The company's contact page names the retail store 'Eggs Hawaii Inc - Island Fresh Eggs' at 419 Waiakamilo Rd (listed as Unit 1E in one place and Unit E1 in another), phone (808) 841-7695. This ties the Star-Advertiser 'Island Fresh Eggs' shop to this business. The company office is at 1590 Hau Street, phone (808) 841-7521. The Facebook page is the business's own. Current hours are not stated on any own page I could read. An older Honolulu Magazine item gave 8:30-3:30 Mon-Fri and 7:30-2 Sat, but it is several years old and directory hours conflict, so schedule_text is null. Honolulu Magazine's March 2025 update still lists the shop at this address. No 2026 own post found, so still_active is null rather than true. Ka Lei eggs are also sold at Kakaʻako Farmers Market (already in the directory).

name: Keiki Construction Zone
notes: The 2026 venue and organizer are not stated in the source I read. Earlier editions: Ke Alaula Farms, Whitmore Village, Wahiawa (Dec 9, 2023, free, per an organizer page by Max Gainz Inc./Ohana Hui Ventures). The 2025 edition was approved on state Agribusiness Development Corporation land in Whitmore Village, with BZ Services LLC as organizer (Environment Hawaiʻi). I did not confirm that 2026 is at the same site, so side and neighborhood are null. Admission changed from free in 2023 to $35 in 2026. Do not confuse with the monthly Hawaiʻi State Public Library 'Keiki Construction Zone' play program. Vendor application and own page not found.

name: Kimchi Festival Hawaiʻi (Kimchi Day Festival)
schedule_text: Annual one-day festival; 2026 edition Saturday, November 14, 2026, 10 AM-7 PM.
organizer: Kimchi Festival Hawaiʻi (earlier editions hosted by The United Korean Association of Hawaii)
notes: Organizer's own page confirms the 2026 date and hours (current, 14 days out). Hawaii Parent's November 2026 calendar matches. The organizer page does not state a 2026 venue. Earlier editions were at Makiki District Park Field, 1527 Keeaumoku St: the 2024 edition per the organizer page and KHON2, and a 2025 edition per Honolulu Magazine. Venue, neighborhood and side are left null until the organizer states it. Free admission was reported by KHON2 for the 2024 edition only. Instagram/Facebook handles not captured.

name: Oahu Fresh (Farmers' Market Box / subscription delivery)
schedule_text: Weekly or biweekly produce bag delivery or pickup at various island pickup locations; the site mentions weekly Wednesday delivery in one member comment. Order cutoffs apply each week.
notes: The live shop page shows current products and prices but is undated. The company's about page lists delivery charges by region (Region 1 $2.50 plus tax, Region 2 $5), but it is an archive page and may be dated. Delivery or pickup options are not captured here. It is a delivery subscription, not a market, so no directory kind fits and kind is null. Weekly bag contents are announced each Monday per Slow Food Oahu. The company runs from the Oahu Food Hub, 916 Kaaahi Place (per a farm directory; not used as a venue). Old press fees: Star-Advertiser 2020 gave a $15 membership and $5-7 delivery. No 2026 post found.

name: Okinawan FEASTival
venue_name: Okinawan-owned restaurants and food businesses across Oʻahu
schedule_text: Annual two-week run of restaurant specials after the Okinawan Festival. The 7th FEASTival ran September 7-21, 2026 (range). The 2027 run has not been announced.
notes: The 2026 run has ended (Sept 21). The two date entries are the start and end of a continuous range, not two separate events. Organizer specials page is titled for the 7th FEASTival, Sept 7-21, 2026; Star-Advertiser (2026-09-02) says the seventh annual run was Sept 7-21 with the full participant list at hawaiiokinawans.com. Honolulu Magazine says 20 restaurants took part. Examples in 2026 coverage: Oide Kitchen (212 Merchant St), Masa & Joyce (Kāneʻohe), Sunrise Restaurant (525 Kapahulu Ave), SKY Waikiki, an Aloha Andagi pop-up at Marukai Dillingham, and Beer Lab Pearlridge. The specials page also carries leftover entries from an earlier edition (for example a Saturday 9/13 sale at Ige's Halawa, which fits 2025, not 2026). I could not verify the conflicting 'November 2 - 8' line from my results, so I treat it as a leftover. The Okinawan Festival itself was Sept 5-6, 2026 at the Hawaii Convention Center. The Facebook page is the festival's, which mentions the FEASTival. still_active is true because the organizer ran the 2026 program and the series is annual.

name: Haleiwa Town Festival
schedule_text: Listed for Saturday, November 14, 2026, 9 AM to 2 PM.
notes: Single aggregator source, and no organizer page was found. The aggregator gives the location as Waialua Community Association, the same venue it gives for a separate Haleiwa Town Art Walk on Nov 7. That does not obviously fit a Haleʻiwa town street festival, so the venue and the street setting are unverified, and the venue_name and times may be copy-forward errors. A different event on the same day is Holoholo to Haleʻiwa, 2-4 PM at the Kamehamalu Courtyard (Haleʻiwa Store Lots); it is not this festival. The Haleiwa Arts Festival (June) and the July 4 festival are separate events. Confirm with the organizer before listing. Admission and hours come from the aggregator only.

name: Ho Farms produce pickup (Ewa Beach / Honolulu)
venue_name: Old Fort Weaver Road (Ewa Beach); Republik (Concert and Event Center) (Honolulu)
schedule_text: Per an undated Sierra Club Oʻahu list: pickup Mondays 3-5 pm on Old Fort Weaver Road (Ewa Beach) and Saturdays 1-3 pm at Republik (Concert and Event Center), Honolulu. Not confirmed as current.
notes: I could not reach a current page on Ho Farms' own site showing these pickups. The same text appears in a Sierra Club blog that the search engine dated to about 2020, and it points to a Local Line ordering page (localline.ca/hofarms). It reads as a pandemic-era online-ordering list. The text does not say whether a subscription or box is offered. The farm's own X account lists hofarms.com as its website, which is the only own-source link I found. Ho Farms produce is also sold through Farm Link Hawaiʻi (a separate seller). Pickup sites are not verified as current, so still_active is null. Do not list until the farm confirms.

name: Kahuku Land Farms Stand
neighborhood: Kahuku (across from Kawela Bay, near Turtle Bay Resort)
schedule_text: A 2017 Star-Advertiser piece said the stands are open daily during daylight hours. Not confirmed as current.
notes: No own website, social account or organizer found. No street address stated by a usable source; the listed '56-800 Kamehameha Hwy' on an aggregator is Kahuku Farms' address, so it was not used. Honolulu Magazine (about Aug 2026) describes browsing 'neighboring stands' next to Kuilima Farm Stand, which suggests roadside stands are still operating there, but it does not name this collective. A Hawaiʻi Life guide (about Mar 2026) lists 'Kahuku Fruit Stands' open daily 9-5 across from Kawela Bay but ties them to Kahuku Farms, which is at a different address. That conflicts with the independent-stand description. Possible overlap with Kuilima Farm Stand (kuilimafarm.com, 57-146 Kamehameha Hwy, open daily 9-5 per Honolulu Magazine); not merged. Check for duplicates with Chue's Farm Fruit Stand and Kahuku Farms. Duplicate of the next row.

name: Kahuku Land Farms Stand (Kahuku fruit stands)
schedule_text: A 2017 Star-Advertiser piece said open daily during daylight hours. Not confirmed as current.
notes: Appears to be a duplicate of the previous row. Same findings: no own page or organizer found, and no usable street address. The Hawaii Life blog post on conservation-easement rules (kahuku-land-farms-fruit-stands-new-rules) was not re-opened. Honolulu Magazine (about Aug 2026) mentions neighboring stands beside Kuilima Farm Stand, but the operator and current hours of this collective are unverified. A 9-5 daily schedule in a recent Hawaiʻi Life guide is attributed there to Kahuku Farms, so it was not used. Check for overlap with Kuilima Farm Stand before listing.

name: Local Inside CSA (Hawaii Agricultural Foundation, HAF Ag Park Kunia)
venue_name: HAF Ag Park, Kunia (produce source); pickup sites around Oʻahu
schedule_text: Older sources describe produce bags with about a dozen pickup sites across Oʻahu. Current schedule and sites not confirmed.
notes: GoFarm Hawaii (a third-party page, search-dated about 2024) says HAF relaunched Local Inside as a platform connecting farmers with the community, previously a CSA program. So the bag and pickup model may no longer run as described. No current page on the organizer's own site was retrieved. The magazine article was dated about 2020-21 by the search engine. The 2020 Star-Advertiser gave localinside.csaware.com. The HAF website is from a directory listing and was not opened. Pickup sites are unverified, so side is null. Not suitable to list as a recurring pickup until HAF confirms.

name: Mahiku Farmers Market
notes: The organizer site exists but the page I could read only gives address and contact (contact named: Sonny Doung; email and phone on page). No current schedule or events found. Weekday hours found on aggregator pages appear to be scraped from map listings, so I did not use them. The 2019 directory entry also listed Hyatt Regency Waikīkī (Tue/Thu) and Mililani (Fri) locations, which are old and unverified. vendorsmap says 'seasonal - contact organizer.' A market-directory page asks whether it is still operating. No evidence it is active in 2026, so still_active is null. Verify with the organizer before publishing.

name: OK Poultry (farm egg sales)
schedule_text: Wednesday and Saturday only, per a food blog about two years old. A farm-directory listing gives 7:30am to 1pm on those days. The blog says to arrive before about 8:30am because eggs sell out. Hours are not confirmed from a current first-party source.
notes: The address and Wed/Sat hours were filled from non-Yelp sources: the Onolicious post (address, phone 808-259-7832, and Instagram instagram.com/okpoultry), the localmeatmilkeggs.org directory, and a Hawaiian Local directory listing. Yelp was not used. A Honolulu Magazine feature (older) confirms the KK Poultry to OK Poultry ownership change and that eggs are sold at the farm. The older Onolicious post mentions a $15 tray of 30 medium white eggs; this is old pricing and not a current price. A Hawaiian Local directory lists okpoultry.com, and Nextdoor lists the business as K K Poultry Farm Inc (same phone). I could not open the website, so the website field is left null. No current first-party page or dated 2026 post was found, so current status is unconfirmed. Waimānalo is windward and borderline for the Honolulu/East scope.

name: Waiahole Farm
notes: Still only a single social mention, which describes it as being on the windward side rather than the North Shore. The TikTok result is a recent social mention, but it does not give an address, hours, or official handle. Address candidates appear only on Yelp and MapQuest, which I did not use. A separate travel blog describes a Waiahole Farm with taro fields, and I could not confirm it is the same business as the fruit stand. No first-party page was found. Needs a first-party source before it goes in the directory. Waiāhole is windward, so side was corrected from the North Shore link in the URL.

name: Waialua Fresh Egg Farm (farm stand)
notes: Sells eggs, not fruit. The farm itself is operating: WATTAgNet (about Aug 2025) reports four new barns under construction, and Civil Beat (2023) reports an active farm. Its own pages describe the farm and brand and do not give stand hours or an address. Stand address and hours appear only on review/map directories, which I excluded, so both are null. Whether the public stand is still open is not confirmed, so still_active is null (farm operating, stand unconfirmed). The farm is jointly owned by Hidden Villa Ranch and Rose Acre Farms (Civil Beat). The earlier-found Facebook page was not re-verified.
